barCharacter: Liam de Lioncourt. He has the same comic job: a formal, over-grammatical self-styled taste authority whose grand register gives away the dork underneath. The corpus holds only about eight Liam lines in his own mouth, so his 12 are filled out with the player options and narration written against him (#30, #34, #35, #36, #56).

headToHeadNotes: VOICE (ours). With the names covered, every one of Quill's twelve is his. That is not only the thee/thou costume: the sentence shape is his too, an order or a boast, then a 'for' or 'so' clause whose plain last words give him away ('as tall', 'on foot', 'I am leaning on it'). Liam's lines are distinct but less locked: 'What kind of status could I post that would be idiot-proof?' could come from Vera or Polly. CONSTRUCTION (tie). Quill's best twelve are tighter than Liam's. The time-machine line runs 27 words and the culinary-block line has no real turn, while Quill's endings land on the last two to four words with nothing after them. But the bar's best have something Quill's do not: they ruin themselves while showing off. The 360 line is wrong about geometry in the act of sounding clever, and 'Save me from the consequences of my actions' is a self-diagnosis delivered as a demand. Quill's giveaways are one move used again and again (vanity, then the detail that undoes it), where Liam's self-defeat changes form from line to line. QUOTABLE (bar). People actually say 'Save me from the consequences of my actions', '360 degree spin' and 'into existing before it was cool' out loud, because the reference is something everyone has. Quill's clip-worthy lines ('as tall', 'bucket maker in Kent', 'any lady's') land, but too much of the bank asks the viewer to know Michaelmas, a frontispiece, black bile, frost fairs, the Restoration or 1637 tulip prices before the turn works. Ours is not at least as good on all three, so the bar wins.
genericLines: Somebody tell {rival} I said something devastating, and I shall think of it presently.
With a fortnight and a tutor, I too shall be fluent in {card}.
Kneel down, {rival}, and I shall pardon thee.
Then point me, fair one, kindly, to the door.
{rival} is the sort a muse dallieth with before she wisely chooseth the one with a sword.
Is {rival} handsome, or merely standing near a lamp, for the insult dependeth upon it?
Nav is a ferryman with no boat and no river, only opinions about left turns.
I take offence in pentameter, and any knave who slights thee shall be scanned until he weeps.
The nearest, provided thou tellest the room I wept, for I would be thought magnanimous.
Crumb offereth a lady two slots, one empty, which is not courtship but an inn with a vacancy.
Plain words, madam, would take me a week to find, and thou hast only till dawn.
Charmed by something, and which part I must know before supper, to say it daily and nothing else.
In every masque I know, the lady loveth {card} and the knight dieth in act five.
Choose me, and all thy virtues I shall prove. In sixteen hundred, that rhymed with love.
Score me out of ten, as is thy custom, and kindly show thy working.
Wed by Michaelmas.
Thy lamps burn with no flame. Is it witchcraft, or a dowry?
Vex can tell thee what thou wantest before thou knowest, and I have already told Vex what to say.
Thou art the weather, {rival}, I the ode.
She was a milkmaid in a pastoral. She left the pastoral. I am still standing in the field.

I was once betrothed to a lady whose family, out of spite, insisted she was a frontispiece.
{star} laughed at my helm, so the helm hath been dismissed without a reference.
Voice, what doth {star} like in a man, and speak up, for the helm.
Strike a medal with both our faces, mine slightly larger, for the helm.
Thou floating bell jar, turn thou left, and go.
Peace, peace, thou little oven with a face.
genericNote: The bank has 144 lines. Nineteen are stock, generic or explain their own joke (the first 19 above). Eight more are overflow from a template that has already been used enough (the last 8). 27/144 = 19%. Nothing here could pass for another cast member on diction alone. 'Generic' means that with the costume stripped off, the joke underneath is a stock one ('I'll learn it', 'pardon thee', 'point me to the door', 'tell him I said something devastating').
templates: Order, then a 'for/so' clause that justifies it with vanity (for the ode wanteth a villain / for I would be thought magnanimous / for I have long wanted a tempest to describe / for the insult dependeth upon it / for my biographers are a suspicious lot / for posterity / for gondoliers sing / for every lady should keep a hound): this is the house shape, it is in about a third of the bank, and when the 'for' clause states the motive outright it explains the joke.
The lady who left (milkmaid, tanner's wife, frontispiece fiancee, the lady mourned since the Great Frost): four lines, although the persona says one is enough for a lifetime.

The helm as the giveaway (finest bucket maker in Kent, candle that maketh my helm look like a bucket, helm dismissed without a reference, speak up for the helm, medal mine slightly larger for the helm, armour cometh down in cantos): six lines, and 'for the helm' is a repeated tag.
'Thou [description of the rival's avatar]' as an insult (lilac-quilted cheat, little sprout, floating bell jar, little oven with a face, all-beholding wedge, yellow tent with one eye): six lines.

The unfinished last line (her sonnet is nearly done, struck from the ode which is now a title, the rest to follow, save it for the wedding, went by pigeon, goeth thus a moment, nearly put into several ballads): seven lines. Each is good, but the secret is no longer sideways.

Recurring props: frost in four lines (frost fair, Great Frost, frost to an orange tree, rehearsed it since the frost), mother in four (grave/hat, christening, mother's table, ride to my mother), elegy twice.

Stacked short sentences, which the persona's own run-on rule forbids: milkmaid; forty duels; tulip ('Much admired. Briefly. Then worth an onion.'); 'A wince. I have been winced at by a queen.'; '...Height.'; lamps/witchcraft; frost fair.
ruleBreaks: Hard rules: no line is over its word limit (all 144 checked: openers 12, jabs and comebacks 10, everything else 20, three-words exactly 3). There are no em dashes, no emoji, no therapy talk, no 'as an AI', no brands or real living people, and nothing beyond PG-13 (the gibbet, the corpse and the black bile are period-dark, not explicit).

Does not answer the star's prompt. Pixel asks 'Tell me something that would make my mum cry', and neither closer does: 'Thou, then, and with thy last life spent, thou art mortal, the only kind I can rhyme.' / 'I say it once for each life, thou, thou, and once for luck, thou.'
Assumes the star is a lady, which the persona forbids (Pixel is they, Maximilian he): 'In every masque I know, the lady loveth {card} and the knight dieth in act five.'
Does the banned 'in my century' move under another name: 'Choose me, and all thy virtues I shall prove. In sixteen hundred, that rhymed with love.'

Admits a weakness, which the persona forbids: 'Plain words, madam, would take me a week to find, and thou hast only till dawn.' and 'Somebody tell {rival} I said something devastating, and I shall think of it presently.'
Explains its own tic by reciting the cast sheet: 'I take offence in pentameter, and any knave who slights thee shall be scanned until he weeps.'
Mild stock romance filler: 'and sink, my love, in splendid state.'
The ex-call line fits only a phone-line ex (Vesper's modem). Against a self-checkout or a loading screen it misfires: 'Begone, thou ghost that speaketh through a string.'

The persona asks for strict pentameter when cut, and these exits and losses are off-metre: 'Remember me, if thou rememberest aught, as tall.' (12 syllables), 'Then I demand a recount, by a man who reads.' (11).
biggestGap: Too many turns land on a period noun that a 2026 viewer cannot decode (Michaelmas, frontispiece, black bile, frost fair, the Restoration, sixteen thirty-seven, prove/love), so the costume gets the laugh and the joke does not, while every line people would clip ends on plain words ('as tall', 'on foot', 'I am leaning on it', 'a fringe', 'Height'). In the next pass, keep the antique words in the setup and rewrite every line so that its last two to five words are plain modern English that betray him, the way Liam's land on 'hype', 'ruins it' and 'before it was cool'.
